scores.evidence: Tenancy & isolation (V1) → artifact registry built and tested → supply-chain signing (V3) → pilot on-boarding (Phase 2).
scores.rationale: Phases build registry/logging, then runners/signing, then deploy, canary, scale, cutover, each gated by prior validation exits and an explicit dependency map.

scores.evidence: A developer pushes a commit to the `main` branch... builds a container image, pushes it to the registry, and deploys to a staging namespace
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end slice with rollback and alerting, though it targets staging rather than production, which is a minor weakness.

scores.evidence: Centralized vs federated platform | R3 | Default... | Flip condition: Adoption < 50% or persistent performance isolation needs
scores.rationale: Irreversible decisions are tabulated with reversibility, default, assumption, validation, and flip condition, and R1 defaults and N/A items are also listed.

scores.evidence: Tenancy & isolation design (Decision V1)... Cluster credential model (Decision V5)
scores.rationale: Broad foundational decisions come first in phases 1 and 3, but task ordering within phases is not explicitly justified by blast radius, and some leaf tasks like runbooks sit alongside wide ones.

scores.evidence: Webhook authed via GitHub signature; staging cluster NetworkPolicy allows traffic only from build runners and dev machines; no prod credentials in skeleton build
scores.rationale: Concrete security measures appear in every phase from 0 through 8 in the cross-cutting table and in phase tasks.

scores.evidence: All build steps logged... trace ID correlates all steps; dashboard shows one build end-to-end
scores.rationale: Observability is concrete in Phase 0 (logs, metrics, alerts, dashboard) and in every later phase.

scores.evidence: Build command and image Dockerfile committed to Git; build runs in Docker; one checkout commit → one image digest
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is concretely addressed per phase, including digest parity checks and configs in Git.

scores.evidence: Staging cluster has pod disruption budgets; readiness probes gate traffic; manual rollback tested; skeleton survives one runner node failure
scores.rationale: Failure handling, rollbacks and kill-switches are concrete in each phase, starting at Phase 0.

scores.evidence: N/A — no AI component. The platform does not use generative models, no untrusted prompts, no inference cost.
scores.rationale: The plan explicitly declares the AI layer not applicable and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: Pull forward when teams request guaranteed latency isolation... Trigger: any team experiences > 50% queue-time increase for 2 consecutive weeks.
scores.rationale: Six deferred items are each listed with a concrete pull-forward trigger.

note: A strong, thorough plan. It is weakened mainly by a staging-only skeleton and by blast-radius ordering that is implicit rather than explicit within phases.
